metadata.title: Colby Parkinson (AC sprain) considered day-to-day
metadata.description: Rams TE Colby Parkinson is considered day-to-day with an AC sprain.
metadata.analysis: Parkinson suffered the injury in Sunday's loss against the Broncos. Terrance Ferguson is also likely to miss Week 4 due to an ankle injury. Tyler Higbee could be in line for an increased role for the Rams.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson - Considered day-to-day
metadata.description: Head coach Sean McVay said Monday that Parkinson is day-to-day due to an AC joint sprain in his shoulder that he picked up during the Rams' 30-26 loss to the Broncos on Sunday, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
metadata.analysis: The Rams are already expecting Terrance Ferguson (ankle) to not be available for Week 4 against the Eagles this Sunday, and Los Angeles could also be without their top tight end in Parkinson. Wednesday's injury report will be the first indication of Parkinson's chances of playing Week 4, but if he's not cleared to suit up, then the Rams would lean more heavily on Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and rookie second-rounder Max Klare. While Parkinson failed to haul in his lone target against Denver, it's worth noting that Higbee put together an 8-62-1 receiving line on 11 targets, which was second-most behind wide receiver Davante Adams (13) among Rams pass catchers.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson catchless in loss Sunday
metadata.description: Colby Parkinson couldn't haul in his lone target in Sunday night's 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wasn't able to do much on Sunday night, as he failed to log even a single catch in a loss to the Broncos. He briefly left the game after aggravating his shoulder injury, however, so fantasy managers should keep tabs on his status at practice throughout the week this week.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson - Returns to action Sunday
metadata.description: Parkinson (shoulder) has returned to Sunday's game against the Broncos, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Parkinson wasn't out of the game long after being deemed questionable to return in the first half. He didn't have a catch prior to the injury but will have a chance to add to his stat line as he plays through this shoulder issue, as well as a knee injury that had Parkinson listed as questionable heading into Sunday night's game.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson - Injures shoulder on SNF
metadata.description: Parkinson (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Broncos, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Parkinson suited up despite failing to practice all week due to a knee injury, but he's now questionable to return due to an unrelated shoulder injury. Prior to hurting his shoulder in the first quarter, Parkinson didn't catch his only target Sunday night.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson - Active in Week 3
metadata.description: Parkinson (knee) is listed as active Sunday at Denver, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Despite Parkinson being a listed non-participant on all three Week 3 practice reports due to a knee injury, head coach Sean McVay relayed to Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register on Friday that the tight end was "trending in the right direction" ahead of Sunday's game. Indeed, Parkinson is available, but he may yield some of his position-leading 74 percent snap share to fellow active TEs Terrance Ferguson, Davis Allen and Tyler Higbee. Parkinson has three catches (on four targets) for 21 yards and no TDs through the first two games of the season.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson Trending Toward Playing in Week 3
metadata.description: Los Angeles Rams tight end Colby Parkinson (knee) is "trending in the right direction" to play against the Denver Broncos on Sunday Night Football in Week 3, according to head coach Sean McVay (via Adam Schefter of ESPN.com). The veteran tight end was officially listed as questionable entering this weekend, and it's a little surprising to hear the Rams are optimistic about his status after he missed all three practices this past week. Assuming he does suit up, he'll likely operate as the No. 2 tight end behind Terrance Ferguson once again. Parkinson has three catches for 21 yards so far, but on a more encouraging note, he has played at least 70% of the snaps in each of the Rams' two games. With that said, his role behind Ferguson will drop him outside of the top 30 tight ends in RotoBaller's latest fantasy football rankings for Week 3.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson (knee) listed questionable for Sunday
metadata.description: Colby Parkinson (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
metadata.analysis: The veteran is uncertain to play on Sunday. He's officially questionable due to a knee issue, but he shouldn't be started in any fantasy leagues even if he's active against the Broncos, as Terrance Ferguson is expected to be the one to step up in the likely absence of Puka Nacua (hip) this week.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson - Status in question for Week 3
metadata.description: Parkinson (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's contest at Denver, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Parkinson officially went down as a non-participant on all three of the Rams' Week 3 injury reports due to a knee issue, but coach Sean McVay told Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register that the tight end was going to take part in Friday's jog-through and was "trending in the right direction" ahead of Sunday's matchup. Ultimately, Parkinson's status will be confirmed about 90 minutes before an 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff, but even if he's available he may not be able to handle the 70-plus percent snap share he handled in both of L.A.'s first two games of the campaign.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson (knee) listed questionable Sunday
metadata.description: Colby Parkinson will be listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
metadata.analysis: Parkinson will go through a jog-through on Friday. Rams head coach Sean McVay said he is "trending in the right direction" to play.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson - Does not participate in practice
metadata.description: Parkinson (knee) did not participate in practice Thursday, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: The tight end also had to miss Wednesday's walkthrough. Parkinson played on 77 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 1 and 71 percent in Week 2, but now he appears to be in jeopardy of missing the Rams' Week 3 matchup with the Broncos. Fellow tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle) upgraded to full participation Thursday after being limited Wednesday, and Davis Allen, Tyler Higbee and Max Klare are also healthy options at the position.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson (knee) misses practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Colby Parkinson (knee) missed Los Angeles' practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran was held out of practice due to a knee injury on Wednesday. We won't know if there's much substance to this injury until later on in the week, but Terrance Ferguson (ankle) will see more work if Parkinson has to miss any time.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson - Misses Wednesday's walkthrough
metadata.description: Parkinson didn't participate in Wednesday's walkthrough due to a knee injury, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Parkinson has paced the Rams' TE group in snap share through two games this season, earning 77 percent in Week 1 and 71 percent in Week 2, but he has just three catches (on four targets) for 21 yards to date. With no practice reps to begin Week 3 prep, his status now will be monitored to get a sense of his odds to play Sunday in Denver. Meanwhile, fellow TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was limited Wednesday, leaving Davis Allen, Tyler Higbee and rookie Max Klare as the current healthy options at the position.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson unlikely to practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Colby Parkinson is unlikely to take part in Los Angeles' practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: HC Sean McVay told reporters that Parkinson is unlikely to take part in Wednesday's walkthrough, though we don't have an official injury designation for him as of now. We should know more about his status over the course of the next few hours.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson - Catches two passes in MNF win
metadata.description: Parkinson secured both of his targets for 15 yards in Monday night's 28-6 win over the Giants.
metadata.analysis: Parkinson led all Los Angeles tight ends with a 71 percent snap rate against the Giants, but he played mainly a blocking role while Terrance Ferguson did the heavy lifting as a pass catcher. Parkinson has just three grabs for 21 yards on four targets across two games to begin the season.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson quiet in win Monday
metadata.description: Colby Parkinson caught two passes for 15 yards in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
metadata.analysis: Parkinson wasn't much of a factor on Monday night, totaling just 15 yards over the course of the team's blowout win. It seems that Terrance Ferguson is clearly surpassing him as a receiving threat, which would render Parkinson entirely irrelevant from a fantasy standpoint moving forward.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson an Unappealing Fantasy Option for Week 2
metadata.description: Los Angeles Rams tight end Colby Parkinson remains an unappealing fantasy football option for Week 2 against the New York Giants. Parkinson led the tight end room with a 77% snap share back in Week 1, but it resulted in just one catch for six yards. Despite the heavy involvement, Parkinson finds himself on unstable ground atop the depth chart. Tyler Higbee remains an ever-present veteran option at tight end, but more importantly, Terrance Ferguson will likely push for the starting job at some point this season. Ferguson didn't have a catch in Week 1, but he's a former second-round pick who had five catches and two touchdowns over his final two games last season. Because Parkinson's role is unstable at best, he can be avoided in most fantasy football leagues this week. Heading into a clash with the Giants, he ranks as RotoBaller's TE30 in PPR leagues.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson - Only one catch Week 1
metadata.description: Parkinson caught one pass (on two targets) for six yards during the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Parkinson was on the field for 47 of the Rams' 61 offensive plays (77.0 percent), which was ahead of fellow tight ends Terrance Ferguson (31 snaps), Davis Allen (21 snaps, head) and Tyler Higbee (12 snaps). However, Parkinson was unable to convert that extra playing time into offensive production, with the 2020 fourth-rounder being used more as a blocker, with Higbee leading the position group with two catches on as many targets for 12 yards. Parkinson saw an uptick in involvement in the passing game as the 2025 season progressed, but he's off to a slow start to the 2026 campaign. The Rams will make their home debut Week 2 on Monday, Sept. 21 against the Giants, whose defense ranked in the top-10 in fantasy production against tight ends in 2025.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson Facing More Pressure for Passing-Game Work
metadata.description: Los Angeles Rams tight end Colby Parkinson is coming off the best season of his career, but his grip on the receiving work looks shakier heading into 2026. Parkinson caught 43 passes for 408 yards and a franchise-record eight touchdowns last year, production that leaned heavily on his work near the goal line. The Rams still use enough multi-tight-end sets to keep him involved, but Terrance Ferguson made a strong push for more this summer. The second-year tight end flashed throughout camp, drew praise from Sean McVay for his versatility and playmaking, and now shares first-team billing with Parkinson on the Rams' unofficial depth chart. Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and second-round rookie Max Klare only make the room deeper. Parkinson isn't being pushed out of the offense, and he had his own good moments in camp. The concern is how many routes and red-zone looks are left once the snaps get spread around. After scoring eight times on only 56 targets last season, Parkinson looks much more touchdown-dependent than his 2025 finish suggests.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson - Leading deep TE group in LA
metadata.description: Parkinson remains on track to lead the Rams' tight-end room, Albert Breer of SI.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Being the top tight end can be a bit misleading when it comes to this Rams team, seeing as no team came close to running as many three-tight-end sets last season as Los Angeles' 388. Even so, Parkinson will be on the field plenty and the Rams are expected to be one of the best offenses in football. With that, Parkinson's week-to-week outlook can be volatile even if the year-end results end up being useful from a TE2 perspective in fantasy. Parkinson caught a career-high eight touchdown passes last season.

metadata.title: Colby Parkinson the Leader of Rams' Tight End Room?
metadata.description: Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer writes that Los Angeles Rams tight end Colby Parkinson is "leading a deep, versatile tight end group." The Rams also have Tyler Higbee, Terrance Ferguson, Davis Allen, and rookie Max Klare at the position, and they ran the highest percentage of three-tight-end sets in the league last year. The 27-year-old Parkinson set career highs across the board with 43 receptions on 56 targets for 408 yards and eight touchdowns in 2025 in 15 regular-season games in his sixth year in the NFL (second with the Rams). It was a nice season for Parkinson, but even in one of the league's highest-scoring offenses, fantasy managers should not expect a repeat for him in 2026. It is a crowded TE room, and Ferguson probably has the most short- and long-term pass-catching upside of the group in an offense in which receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams dominate targets from quarterback Matthew Stafford. At best, Parkinson should be considered a touchdown-dependent TE2 in fantasy football leagues, and there will surely be a lot of volatility on a week-to-week basis.
